examples.en: My grandmother's back is quite bent.

examples.ko: 철사 끝이 꼬부라져서 잘 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The end of the wire is bent, so it won't go in easily.
The road bends to the left up ahead.
I picked up a stick with a bent end.
As people get older, their backs can become stooped.

examples.ko: 머리카락 끝이 꼬부라지지 않게 펴 주세요.
examples.en: Please straighten it so the ends of the hair don't curl.

explain: '구부러지다'와 비슷한 말이에요. 허리, 철사, 길이 휘어진 모습에 쓰고, '꼬부랑 할머니'처럼 허리가 굽은 모습을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '구부러지다'. It describes a back, a wire or a road that bends, and it also appears in '꼬부랑 할머니', an old woman with a bent back.

examples.ko: 가방에 오래 넣어 둬서 바지가 꾸깃꾸깃해요.
examples.en: The pants are all wrinkled from being in the bag for so long.
Shops accept even crumpled bills.

examples.ko: 옷이 꾸깃꾸깃해지지 않게 잘 개어 두세요.
examples.en: Fold the clothes well so they don't get wrinkled.
I went to the interview wearing a wrinkled shirt.
The paper got wet in the rain and became crumpled.
I unfolded the crumpled letter and read it.

explain: 주름이 많이 잡혀 구겨진 상태를 나타내서 옷, 종이, 지폐에 자주 써요. 구기는 동작은 '꾸기다', 이미 구겨진 상태는 '꾸깃꾸깃하다'로 말해요. '구깃구깃하다'보다 센 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes a state with many creases, so it fits clothes, paper and banknotes. The action of crumpling is '꾸기다', while the already-crumpled state is '꾸깃꾸깃하다'. It sounds stronger than '구깃구깃하다'.

examples.en: The host came out wearing a black bow tie.
Please tell me how to tie a bow tie.
I bought a bow tie for my son's graduation ceremony.
You look sharp with a bow tie on your suit.
Your bow tie is slightly crooked.
The waiters are all wearing bow ties.

explain: 넥타이는 목에 '매다'라고 하고 나비넥타이도 '매다'나 '하다'를 써요. '나비'는 곤충 나비 모양을 닮아서 붙은 말이에요. 파티, 결혼식, 공연처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 주로 봐요.
explain_en: A necktie is something you '매다' (tie), and with a bow tie you can use either '매다' or '하다'. '나비' (butterfly) is in the name because of its shape. You mostly see it at formal events such as parties, weddings, and performances.

examples.en: I have astigmatism, so I wear glasses.
The letters look blurry because of astigmatism.
You can get astigmatism checked at an eye clinic.

examples.ko: 동생은 난시가 심해서 밤 운전을 못 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has severe astigmatism and can't drive at night.
I got new lenses for astigmatism.
At my eye test I was told I have astigmatism.

explain: 눈 이야기에서 '근시'는 먼 곳이 흐리게 보이는 것, '원시'는 가까운 곳이 흐리게 보이는 것이고 난시는 물체가 겹치거나 번져 보이는 거예요. 안경 처방에서 '난시가 있다'고 해요.
explain_en: Among eye conditions, 근시 blurs far objects and 원시 blurs near ones, while 난시 makes things look doubled or smeared. In a prescription you say '난시가 있다'.

examples.en: The baby has started to use the toilet on his own.
You need to toilet-train the puppy.
At the hospital they also check the patient's urine and stool output.
The child who had been holding it in ran to the bathroom.

examples.ko: 고양이 대소변은 매일 치워 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to clean up the cat's waste every day.

examples.ko: 대소변 문제로 걱정되면 병원에 가 보세요.
examples.en: If you're worried about bowel or urinary problems, go see a doctor.

explain: 대변과 소변을 함께 부르는 말이에요. 아이, 환자, 반려동물을 돌보는 상황에서 자주 쓰고 '대소변을 가리다'가 대표적인 짝이에요. 어린아이에게는 '응가', '쉬'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to feces and urine together. It is often used when caring for children, patients, or pets, and '대소변을 가리다' is the typical pairing. With small children people say '응가' and '쉬'.

examples.en: Today the stars are clearly visible even to the naked eye.

examples.ko: 이 벌레는 너무 작아서 맨눈으로 보기 어려워요.
examples.en: This bug is so small that it's hard to see with the naked eye.

examples.ko: 맨눈으로 일식을 보면 눈이 다칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: Watching an eclipse with the naked eye can hurt your eyes.

examples.ko: 안경을 벗으면 맨눈 시력이 아주 나빠요.
examples.en: Without my glasses, my uncorrected eyesight is very bad.
There's also a lot of dust that's hard to confirm with the naked eye.
The colors look different even with the naked eye.

explain: 안경, 망원경, 현미경 같은 도구 없이 눈만으로 본다는 뜻이에요. 대부분 '맨눈으로'의 형태로 나와요. 같은 뜻의 한자어 '육안'은 뉴스나 설명문에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It means seeing with your eyes alone, without glasses, a telescope or a microscope. It mostly appears as '맨눈으로'. The Sino-Korean word '육안' has the same meaning and shows up more in news and explanatory writing.

examples.en: My knees ache, so stairs scare me.

examples.ko: 달리기를 한 뒤로 발목이 계속 시큰시큰해요.
examples.en: My ankle has kept aching since I went running.
I massaged my aching shoulder and it got a bit better.
If your teeth keep feeling sensitive, go see a dentist.
My wrist aches, but I have to work.
My nose stung at the moving scene.

explain: '시큰하다'를 되풀이해서 시큰한 느낌이 계속 이어지는 모습을 나타내요. 관절이나 이의 통증 외에 코끝이 찡할 때도 써요. 하나의 순간적인 느낌보다는 이어지는 느낌에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It repeats '시큰하다' to show the sore or stinging feeling continuing. Besides pain in joints or teeth, it can describe a stinging nose when moved. It suits a lingering feeling better than a single momentary one.

examples.ko: 의사가 이 병은 완치할 수 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said this illness can be completely cured.
Grandfather fully recovered from pneumonia and left the hospital.

examples.ko: 큰 병은 완치하는 데 몇 년이 걸리기도 해요.
examples.en: For a serious illness, it can take years to be fully cured.

examples.ko: 완치해도 정기 검사는 계속 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Even after full recovery, you must keep getting regular checkups.
I heard the story of a person who beat cancer completely.
My friend has finally fully recovered.

explain: '낫다'는 아프던 것이 좋아질 때 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '완치하다'는 병이 완전히 없어질 때 병원이나 뉴스에서 써요. '완치되다'도 많이 써요. 치료가 다 끝났다는 느낌이라서 가벼운 증상에는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: '낫다' is the everyday word for getting better; '완치하다' means a disease is completely gone and appears in hospitals and news. '완치되다' is also common. It implies treatment is finished, so it is rarely used for minor symptoms.

examples.en: My grandmother is recuperating in the countryside.

examples.ko: 수술 후에 한 달 동안 집에서 요양했어요.
examples.en: After the surgery, I recuperated at home for a month.
I recuperate in the mountains to regain my health.
You have to take a break from work while you recuperate.
Thanks to a long recovery, I got much better.

examples.ko: 몸이 나을 때까지 병원에서 요양할 거예요.
examples.en: I will recuperate in the hospital until I get better.

explain: '쉬다'는 가벼운 휴식이고, '요양하다'는 아프거나 수술한 뒤 몸이 낫도록 오래 조용히 지내는 거예요. 보통 '시골에서 요양하다', '집에서 요양하다'처럼 장소와 같이 써요. 노인을 돌보는 시설은 '요양원'이에요.
explain_en: 쉬다 is a light rest, while 요양하다 is staying quietly for a long time so that the body can heal after an illness or surgery. It is usually used with a place, as in '시골에서 요양하다'. A facility that cares for the elderly is a 요양원.

examples.en: The child said he wanted to go to the toilet.
We stopped the bus and relieved ourselves for a moment.
The puppy does its business in the designated spot.
I needed the toilet badly, so I ran to the restroom.
I always wash my hands after using the toilet.
When do you start potty training a baby?

explain: '용변을 보다'로 쓰고, 화장실 가는 일을 직접 말하지 않고 점잖게 돌려 말하는 표현이에요. 아기나 반려동물 이야기, 안내문에서 자주 나와요. 친구끼리는 보통 '화장실 가다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used as '용변을 보다', a polite, indirect way to talk about going to the toilet. It often appears in talk about babies and pets and on signs. Among friends people usually just say '화장실 가다'.

examples.ko: 이 병은 전염성이 강해서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: This disease is highly contagious, so you need to be careful.
Colds are contagious too, so please wear a mask.

examples.ko: 전염성 높은 병에 걸리면 집에서 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: If you catch a highly contagious illness, you must rest at home.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 전염성을 확인하려고 검사를 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor ran a test to check whether it was contagious.

examples.ko: 전염성에 대한 뉴스를 보고 걱정이 됐어요.
examples.en: I watched the news about contagiousness and got worried.

examples.ko: 그 병은 전염성도 약하고 증상도 가벼워요.
examples.en: That illness is weakly contagious and the symptoms are mild.

explain: '전염성이 강하다', '전염성이 높다', '전염성이 약하다'처럼 써요. 감기처럼 흔한 병은 '옮다'를 더 많이 써서 '감기가 옮았어요'라고 해요. 하품이나 기분이 퍼질 때도 '전염되다'를 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as '전염성이 강하다' (very contagious), '높다', or '약하다'. For common illnesses like colds, people usually say '옮다', as in '감기가 옮았어요'. '전염되다' can also describe yawns or moods spreading.

examples.en: The sun beats down hot on the crown of my head.
The top of the child's head smells like a baby.
The top of my head is thinning, so I wear a hat often.
I hit the door and the top of my head hurt.

examples.ko: 미용사가 정수리 쪽 머리를 더 잘랐어요.
examples.en: The hairdresser cut more hair on the top of my head.
My mom kissed the top of my head.

explain: 정수리는 머리 맨 위의 가운데 부분이에요. 머리 앞쪽은 '이마', 뒤쪽은 '뒤통수'라고 해서 위치마다 이름이 달라요. 머리숱이나 샴푸, 햇볕 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 정수리 is the very top center of the head. The front is '이마' and the back is '뒤통수', so each area has its own name. It comes up often in talk of hair volume, shampoo and sunlight.

examples.en: The sun was strong, so I put on arm sleeves.
You need arm covers when doing farm work.

examples.ko: 자전거용 토시는 팔을 시원하게 해 줘요.
examples.en: Cycling arm sleeves keep your arms cool.
I bought gloves and arm sleeves too.
How much is a pair of arm sleeves?
Sweat built up inside the arm sleeves, so I took them off.

explain: 토시는 손목에서 팔꿈치 사이만 덮어요. 햇빛을 막거나 일할 때 소매를 보호하려고 써요. 장갑과 달리 손가락은 덮지 않아요. 입는 게 아니라 '끼다'나 '하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 토시 covers only the forearm, between the wrist and the elbow. It is worn to block the sun or to protect the sleeves while working. Unlike gloves, it does not cover the fingers. It is not 입다 but 끼다 or 하다.
